checks: Real OPFS float WAV commit has exact metadata, headers, sample count and independently convolved PCM
Cached readers zero-pad outside the song without moving actual samples
Unfinished cache cannot be recalled; abort removes its actual OPFS directory
Failed append can be aborted without leaving a partially published stem pair
A damaged float WAV header rejects despite the correct file length
A truncated stem rejects before any preview or analysis read
Non-finite cached float samples are sanitized by the WAV reader
Stored metadata must match project source identity and reject corrupted JSON
Caller metadata requires a finite numeric duration
Stored metadata requires matching version, key and physically consistent duration
Explicit discard removes a completed cache and makes stale recall unavailable
Actual OPFS cache survives page reload and returns the identical float sample and count.
A genuine browser worker creates, commits and reads separated float PCM through OPFS.
limits: Real desktop Chromium OPFS and workers; not Android filesystem or physical phone execution.
Analytical FIR and synthetic PCM validate transport clocks and fidelity, not musical recognition.
